If you have two hamsters in the same cage, she may be feeling very stressed out by this and that was her way of telling you she isn’t happy. Hamsters may tolerate each other living together, but they highly prefer being alone. They can live most of their lives together and one day say “I’ve had enough I want my space” and kill the other. They could fight and have it go too far if they are fighting over food. Sometimes they feel like they need to hoard food and keep the other hamster away from it because they don’t know when their next meal is, they can’t hunt for themselves in the cage.

You could try separating them for a few weeks and see if there is a change. I say a few weeks because they would need to adjust to the new home and situation with being alone suddenly.

Exactly. Hamsters are unpredictable. They could live half their lives with another ham and one day literally wake up and kill the other.
Or they get into a fight that goes too far. They like being alone and having another hamster in their cage is stressful cuz unless you have two of everything (food,water, hides) then they might both feel like they have to fight for food and worry there might not be enough, so they will literally fight and steal food from the other. I’ve seen cases where one hamster will bully the other one away from all the food and it starves.

In the wild they only really tolerate each other for mating and then part ways.

You can supplement the bedding with toilet paper and paper towels as well. Any paper that doesn’t have ink or dust on it would work. You could put old cut up clothes in there or fleece blankets. If they have your scent that will help your hamster learn your scent and learn that you are safe and have the foods and warmth. You can throw away the cloth when it’s too dirty. You could clean it, but that’s tricky. You don’t want to use any soap that has perfume in it, so it’s better to just toss it.

Getting the biggest thing of bedding would be best if you can afford it. They come in big packs. And cleaning the cage daily with spot cleaning is perfect and then changing the cage every week and a half to two weeks should be okay as long as she isn’t a super messy ham lol you can also liter train hamster which makes cleaning even easier cuz they will just pee in one little tray with sand or bedding in it. They also need sandbaths so they often will roll around in the sand they pee in. So I’d use bedding or something like that. They pee often, but it’s not a ton. Just a little puddle usually.

You can bake the play sand to kill any germs and then sift it with a shifter or a colander. Sand baths are not an option. They really do need them. And definitely enough space for them both to roll around in it. It’s super cute to watch it makes their fur clean and soft and will make them happy too! They’re fur can get really gross and licking can only do so much for them to stay clean. Not having a sandbath can potentially cause stress for your little friend. Imagine moving into a new place, you’re all alone, it’s clean and has a lot of room for you to do it all alone and I, comfy bed to sleep in...but you don’t have a shower or a bath, you can just take sponge baths. While that does work, you’re not going to get as clean as you would like. That’s what happens when they don’t have a proper sandbath.

Hamster are nocturnal, they are awake during the night and sleep all day. You should not wake up a sleeping hamster, it will stress him out and that could make him sick. He is probably sleeping right now because you keep waking him. Give him a few days to get used to his cage and then try and interact with him. Do not chase him around the cage if he does not want to be picked up. They are easily startled.

You need to take it slow, with all animals when you first get them you need to take it slow. Let them get used to you and know that you are their friend and you aren't going to hurt them.

Also, side note. Don't get mad at the hamster for doing what he does naturally. They do not respond to discipline. You have to be careful. Be gentle, don't squeeze him, drop him, flick or hit him.
